lesson.heading: Eligibility and conditions: section 16
lesson.body:
Section 16(1): a registered person may take credit of input tax charged on supply of goods or services used or intended to be used **in the course or furtherance of business**. The amount is credited to the electronic credit ledger.

Section 16(2) conditions, all of which must be met:
- (a) He holds a tax invoice or debit note (or other prescribed document).
- (aa) Details of the invoice or debit note are furnished by the supplier in GSTR-1 and communicated to the recipient (GSTR-2B).
- (b) He has **received** the goods or services. In bill-to-ship-to cases, goods delivered to a third person on his direction are deemed received. Goods received in lots: ITC on receipt of the last lot.
- (ba) Details of ITC are not restricted in the statement communicated under section 38.
- (c) Tax charged has actually been paid to the Government by the supplier, in cash or through utilisation of admissible ITC.
- (d) He has furnished his return under section 39.

**180-day rule (second proviso to 16(2), rule 37):** if the recipient does not pay the supplier the value and tax within **180 days** from the invoice date, ITC proportionate to the unpaid amount is added to his output tax liability with interest. It can be re-availed on payment. This does not apply to RCM supplies or deemed supplies without consideration.

**Section 16(3):** no ITC on the tax component of capital goods if depreciation has been claimed on it under the Income-tax Act.

**Section 16(4) time limit:** ITC on an invoice or debit note cannot be taken after the **30 November** following the end of the FY to which the invoice or debit note relates, or the date of filing the annual return, whichever is earlier.

lesson.heading: Apportionment: section 17(1), 17(2) and rule 42
lesson.body:
Where goods or services are used partly for business and partly for other purposes, ITC is restricted to the business portion (17(1)). Where used partly for taxable (including zero-rated) supplies and partly for exempt supplies, ITC is restricted to the taxable portion (17(2)).

Rule 42, simplified for common inputs and input services:

| Step | Treatment |
| --- | --- |
| T1 | ITC used exclusively for non-business purposes - not allowed |
| T2 | ITC used exclusively for exempt supplies - not allowed |
| T3 | ITC blocked under 17(5) - not allowed |
| T4 | ITC used exclusively for taxable supplies - fully allowed |
| C2 | Common credit |
| D1 | Reversal for exempt supplies = C2 x E / F (E = exempt turnover, F = total turnover in the State) |
| D2 | Reversal for non-business use = 5% of C2 |

For this purpose, value of exempt supply (section 17(3)) includes supplies on which the recipient pays tax under RCM, transactions in securities, sale of land and, subject to para 5 of Schedule II, sale of building.

lesson.heading: Blocked credits: section 17(5)
lesson.body:
| Clause | ITC not available on | Exceptions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a), (aa), (ab) | Motor vehicles for transport of persons with seating capacity up to 13 (including driver); vessels and aircraft; and their general insurance, servicing, repair and maintenance | Used for further supply of such vehicles, transport of passengers, imparting training on driving; goods transport vehicles are not blocked |
| (b)(i) | Food and beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, cosmetic and plastic surgery, leasing or renting of blocked vehicles, life and health insurance | Used for making an outward taxable supply of the same category or as an element of a taxable composite or mixed supply; or obligatory for an employer to provide to employees under any law |
| (b)(ii), (iii) | Membership of a club, health and fitness centre; travel benefits to employees on vacation such as leave travel concession | Obligatory under law for the employer |
| (c), (d) | Works contract services and goods or services for construction of an immovable property on own account (other than plant and machinery), to the extent capitalised | Works contract used as input for further works contract service |
| (e) | Goods or services on which tax is paid under composition | - |
| (fa) | Goods or services used for activities under corporate social responsibility (section 135 Companies Act) | - |
| (g) | Goods or services for personal consumption | - |
| (h) | Goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off, or disposed of by way of gift or free samples | - |
| (i) | Tax paid in pursuance of orders for fraud or wilful misstatement, and on goods detained or confiscated (sections 129, 130) | - |

'Construction' includes re-construction, renovation, additions, alterations or repairs **to the extent capitalised**. Repairs charged to profit and loss are not blocked.

lesson.heading: Worked example and common mistakes
lesson.body:
Common input services carry GST of ₹1,20,000. Exempt turnover is ₹30 lakh and total turnover in the State is ₹1.2 crore.

| Particulars | ₹ |
| --- | --- |
| Common credit C2 | 1,20,000 |
| Reversal D1 = 1,20,000 x 30/120 | 30,000 |
| Eligible common credit | 90,000 |

**Common mistakes:**
- Blocking ITC on a goods truck. Only passenger vehicles up to 13 seats are blocked.
- Allowing ITC on capital goods where depreciation was claimed on the GST component (section 16(3)).
- Allowing ITC on invoices not reflected in GSTR-2B: section 16(2)(aa) requires this.
- Blocking ITC on repairs of a factory building charged to revenue: only capitalised construction is blocked.
- Forgetting that ITC on goods given as free samples or lost in fire is blocked.

keyPoints: Section 16(2): invoice, GSTR-2B reflection, receipt, tax paid by supplier, own return filed.
Unpaid supplier beyond 180 days from invoice: reverse proportionate ITC with interest; re-avail on payment.
Section 16(3): no ITC on the tax component if depreciation is claimed on it.
Section 16(4): ITC deadline is the earlier of 30 November after the FY end and annual return filing.
Rule 42: reversal for exempt supplies = common credit x exempt turnover / total turnover.
Section 17(5) blocks: passenger vehicles up to 13 seats, food and catering, clubs, LTC, construction (capitalised), composition tax, CSR, personal use, goods lost or gifted.
Exceptions: same-category outward taxable supply, or employer obligation under law.

questions.prompt: An invoice dated 10 March 2026 (FY 2025-26) was missed in the books. The company files its annual return for FY 2025-26 on 15 October 2026. By what date can ITC on this invoice be claimed at the latest?
options: 30 November 2026
15 October 2026
31 March 2027
31 December 2026
questions.explanation: Section 16(4): earlier of 30 November following the end of the FY (30 November 2026) and the date of furnishing the annual return (15 October 2026). The earlier date, 15 October 2026, applies.

questions.prompt: ITC on which of the following is blocked under section 17(5)?
options: A 7-seater car bought by a driving school to train learners
A 5-seater car bought by a company for its directors
A truck used to deliver goods
A 20-seater bus used to transport employees
questions.explanation: Motor vehicles for transport of persons with seating up to 13 are blocked unless used for further supply of vehicles, passenger transport or driving training. The driving school car falls in an exception; the truck carries goods; the bus has more than 13 seats.

questions.prompt: A company has 300 workers and the Factories Act requires it to run a canteen. GST on canteen services is ₹50,000. ITC is:
options: Blocked
Available, because providing the service is obligatory under law
Available only to the extent recovered from employees
Available at 50%
questions.explanation: The proviso to section 17(5)(b) allows ITC on food and beverages, catering and similar services where it is obligatory for an employer to provide them to employees under any law in force.

questions.prompt: GST paid on repairs to a factory building, charged to the profit and loss account and not capitalised, is blocked under section 17(5)(d).
questions.explanation: The Explanation to section 17(5) defines construction to include repairs only to the extent of capitalisation. Repairs expensed to revenue are not blocked.

questions.prompt: Fill the blank: if the recipient does not pay the supplier within ___ days from the date of invoice, proportionate ITC must be added to his output tax liability with interest.
questions.explanation: Second proviso to section 16(2) read with the CGST Rules: ITC on unpaid amounts after 180 days from the invoice is reversed with interest and can be re-availed on payment.

questions.prompt: GST on common input services is ₹1,20,000. Exempt turnover is ₹30,00,000 and total turnover in the State is ₹1,20,00,000. Compute the ITC to be reversed under rule 42 for exempt supplies. Round to the nearest rupee.

A recipient took full ITC of ₹90,000 on an invoice of ₹5,90,000 (value ₹5,00,000 + GST ₹90,000). Within 180 days he paid only ₹2,95,000 to the supplier. Compute the ITC to be reversed. Round to the nearest rupee.

ITC is reversed in proportion to the amount not paid (value plus tax).

| Particulars | ₹ |
| --- | --- |
| Unpaid amount 5,90,000 - 2,95,000 | 2,95,000 |
| Reversal = 90,000 x 2,95,000 / 5,90,000 | 45,000 |

Interest is also payable, and the credit can be re-availed when he pays.

questions.prompt: State the conditions to be fulfilled for availing input tax credit under section 16 of the CGST Act.
questions.answer:
- The person must be registered and the goods or services must be used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of business (16(1)).
- Possession of a tax invoice or debit note or other prescribed document (16(2)(a)).
- Details of the invoice or debit note furnished by the supplier in GSTR-1 and communicated in GSTR-2B (16(2)(aa)).
- Receipt of goods or services; deemed receipt in bill-to-ship-to and services provided to another person on his direction; for lots, credit on the last lot (16(2)(b)).
- ITC not restricted in the section 38 statement (16(2)(ba)).
- Tax actually paid by the supplier to the Government (16(2)(c)).
- Return under section 39 furnished (16(2)(d)).
- Payment to supplier within 180 days, else reversal with interest.
- No ITC on tax component if depreciation is claimed on it (16(3)); time limit under 16(4).

questions.prompt: ITC on motor vehicles is blocked under section 17(5)(a). Explain the scope of this restriction and its exceptions.
questions.answer:
- Blocked: motor vehicles for transportation of persons with approved seating capacity of not more than 13 persons including the driver.
- Exceptions: where used for making further taxable supply of such vehicles (a car dealer), transportation of passengers (a taxi operator), or imparting training on driving such vehicles (a driving school).
- Vehicles for transport of goods and passenger vehicles with seating above 13 are not blocked.
- Clause (ab) blocks general insurance, servicing, repair and maintenance of blocked vehicles, with the same exceptions, and also allows ITC to manufacturers and insurers in specified cases.
- Clause (b)(i) blocks leasing, renting or hiring of such vehicles unless used for the same category of outward supply or obligatory for an employer under law.

chapters.title: Registration
chapters.summary: Who must register under GST: threshold-based registration under section 22, persons not liable under section 23, compulsory registration under section 24, the procedure, special persons, and cancellation and revocation.
chapters.lawAsOf: CGST Act sections 22 to 30 and related rules and threshold notifications, as amended by the Finance Act 2026

lesson.heading: Threshold for registration: section 22 and aggregate turnover
lesson.body:
A supplier must register in the State or UT from where he makes taxable supplies if his **aggregate turnover** in a financial year exceeds the threshold:

| Supplier | Normal States | Special category States |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Supplier of services, or of goods and services | ₹20 lakh | ₹10 lakh (Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura) |
| Exclusive supplier of goods (Notification 10/2019-CT), if the State has adopted it | ₹40 lakh | Not available; ₹20 lakh or ₹10 lakh applies |

The ₹40 lakh limit is not available to suppliers of ice cream, pan masala and tobacco products, and is not adopted by certain States (mainly North-Eastern and hill States); the ₹20 lakh limit applies there.

**Aggregate turnover (section 2(6))**: the aggregate value of all taxable supplies (excluding inward supplies taxed under RCM), exempt supplies, exports, and inter-State supplies between distinct persons having the **same PAN**, computed on an **all-India basis**, excluding CGST, SGST, UTGST, IGST and cess.

| Included | Excluded |
| --- | --- |
| Taxable supplies (forward charge) | Value of inward supplies on which tax is paid under RCM |
| Exempt supplies, including non-taxable supplies such as alcoholic liquor | GST and cess |
| Exports (zero-rated) | Activities in Schedule III (not supplies) |
| Supplies by all branches with the same PAN across India | For an agriculturist: supply of produce from own cultivation |

lesson.heading: Persons not liable and compulsory registration
lesson.body:
**Section 23 - not liable to register:**
- Persons engaged exclusively in supplying goods or services not liable to tax or wholly exempt.
- An agriculturist, for supply of produce out of cultivation of land.
- Persons notified by the Government, such as those making only supplies on which the recipient pays tax under RCM, and persons making inter-State supplies of taxable services with aggregate turnover within the threshold.

**Section 24 - compulsory registration irrespective of turnover:**
- Persons making inter-State taxable supply of goods (inter-State services up to the threshold are exempted by notification).
- Casual taxable persons making taxable supply.
- Persons required to pay tax under reverse charge.
- Persons required to pay tax under section 9(5) (ECOs).
- Non-resident taxable persons.
- Persons required to deduct TDS under section 51.
- Persons making taxable supply on behalf of other taxable persons as agents.
- Input Service Distributors.
- Persons supplying goods or services through an ECO that is required to collect TCS (subject to notified exceptions).
- Every ECO required to collect TCS under section 52.
- Persons supplying online information and database access or retrieval (OIDAR) services from outside India to unregistered persons in India.

lesson.heading: Procedure, GSTIN and special persons
lesson.body:
- **Time limit (section 25):** apply within **30 days** from the date of becoming liable. A casual or non-resident taxable person applies at least **5 days** before commencing business.
- **State-wise registration:** a person registers in each State or UT from where he makes taxable supplies. He may take separate registrations for multiple places of business within a State.
- **Voluntary registration:** allowed even below the threshold; all provisions then apply.
- **PAN** is mandatory (except for non-resident taxable persons, who may use other documents). Registration is subject to Aadhaar authentication or physical verification.
- **GSTIN** is 15 characters: 2-digit State code, 10-character PAN, 1 entity number, 'Z' by default, 1 check digit.

| Special person | Validity | Advance deposit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Casual taxable person | Period in application or 90 days, whichever earlier; extendable by up to 90 days | Amount equal to estimated tax liability for the period |
| Non-resident taxable person | Same as above | Same as above |

**Cancellation (section 29):** by the proper officer (for contravention, non-filing of returns, fraud) or on application by the person (closure, transfer, no longer liable). **Revocation (section 30):** apply within 90 days of the cancellation order where cancelled by the officer; the time can be extended by the prescribed authority. Final return GSTR-10 is due within 3 months of cancellation.

lesson.heading: Worked example and common mistakes
lesson.body:
Mr A (Delhi) reports for the year:

| Particulars | ₹ | Included in aggregate turnover? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Intra-State taxable supplies | 12,00,000 | Yes |
| Exempt supplies (fresh vegetables) | 5,00,000 | Yes |
| Export of services | 4,00,000 | Yes |
| Inward supplies taxed under RCM | 2,00,000 | No |
| GST charged on outward supplies | 2,16,000 | No |
| Taxable supplies by his Haryana branch (same PAN) | 3,00,000 | Yes |
| **Aggregate turnover** | **24,00,000** | Exceeds ₹20 lakh: liable |

**Common mistakes:**
- Excluding exempt supplies or exports from aggregate turnover.
- Using the ₹40 lakh limit for a person who supplies any service, even a small amount: the ₹20 lakh limit applies.
- Computing turnover State-wise. It is computed on an all-India basis for the same PAN.
- Forgetting that a single inter-State sale of taxable goods requires compulsory registration.

keyPoints: Threshold: ₹20 lakh (₹10 lakh in Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura); ₹40 lakh for exclusive goods suppliers in States that adopted it.
Aggregate turnover: taxable + exempt + exports + inter-State supplies of same-PAN branches, all-India, excluding GST and RCM inward supplies.
Section 24: inter-State goods suppliers, casual and non-resident persons, RCM payers, ECOs, TDS deductors, ISDs, agents, OIDAR suppliers register irrespective of turnover.
Apply within 30 days of becoming liable; casual and non-resident persons at least 5 days before starting.
Casual taxable person: validity up to 90 days, extendable by 90 days, advance deposit of estimated tax.
GSTIN: 15 characters - State code (2), PAN (10), entity number, Z, check digit.
Revocation of cancellation: apply within 90 days of the cancellation order.

cases.body:

questions.prompt: Mr Joseph of Kochi (Kerala, a State that has adopted the ₹40 lakh limit) supplies only taxable goods within Kerala with turnover of ₹36 lakh. He also earns ₹3 lakh from repair services. Is he liable to register?

Yes, because he also supplies services, so the ₹20 lakh limit applies and his turnover of ₹39 lakh exceeds it
No, because services up to ₹5 lakh are ignored
Yes, but only for the services
questions.explanation: The ₹40 lakh limit is only for persons engaged exclusively in supply of goods. Any supply of services brings him under the ₹20 lakh limit. Aggregate turnover of ₹39 lakh exceeds it.

A person required to pay tax under reverse charge
An agriculturist selling his own produce
A doctor providing only exempt health care services

questions.prompt: Fill the blank: a person liable to register must apply within ___ days from the date on which he becomes liable.
questions.explanation: Section 25(1). Casual and non-resident taxable persons apply at least 5 days before commencing business.

options: Within 30 days from 10 January 2027, when its aggregate turnover crossed ₹40 lakh
Before 1 April 2026
Only at the end of FY 2026-27
Within 90 days from 10 January 2027

| Estimated tax @ 18% (CGST 9% + SGST 9%) | 1,44,000 |

questions.prompt: Suppose Bloom had not crossed the threshold by March 2027. What is the effect of the Mumbai order?
options: No effect, as turnover is below ₹40 lakh
It must register compulsorily under section 24, because it will make an inter-State taxable supply of goods
The Mumbai buyer will pay tax under reverse charge
It must register in Maharashtra only
questions.explanation: Section 24(i) requires registration for persons making inter-State taxable supplies of goods, irrespective of turnover. Registration is taken in Gujarat, from where the supply is made.

questions.prompt: Examine whether each person is liable to register under the CGST Act. Assume a normal State with a ₹20 lakh limit for services and ₹40 lakh for exclusive goods suppliers.
questions.data:
- (a) An individual farmer selling wheat grown on his own land; turnover ₹55 lakh.
- (b) A freelance designer in Pune providing services only to clients in other States; turnover ₹14 lakh.
- (c) A trader of garments with intra-State turnover of ₹8 lakh who buys goods from an unregistered person and is not liable under RCM.
- (d) A company that receives sponsorship services and pays GST under RCM; its own outward supplies are exempt.
- (e) A Singapore company that sets up a stall at a trade fair in Delhi for 15 days.
questions.answer:
| Case | Liable? | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) | No | Section 23(1)(b): agriculturist supplying produce out of cultivation of land |
| (b) | No | Inter-State supplies of services are exempted from compulsory registration up to the threshold; turnover ₹14 lakh is below ₹20 lakh |
| (c) | No | Turnover below threshold; no section 24 category applies |
| (d) | Yes | Section 24(iii): person required to pay tax under RCM, irrespective of turnover |
| (e) | Yes | Section 24(v): non-resident taxable person; apply at least 5 days before starting, with advance deposit |

questions.prompt: Who is a casual taxable person? Explain the special provisions relating to the registration of casual taxable persons.
questions.answer:
- Section 2(20): a person who occasionally undertakes transactions involving supply of goods or services in the course or furtherance of business, as principal, agent or otherwise, in a State or UT where he has no fixed place of business.
- Must register under section 24 irrespective of turnover (exemption is available for specified handicraft suppliers).
- Apply at least 5 days before commencement of business (section 25(1)).
- Registration is valid for the period in the application or 90 days from the effective date, whichever is earlier; the proper officer may extend it by up to 90 days on request (section 27(1)).
- Must make an advance deposit equal to the estimated tax liability for the period; additional deposit is required on seeking extension (section 27(2)).
- Cannot opt for composition.

questions.prompt: Explain the meaning of aggregate turnover under section 2(6) and its relevance under GST.
questions.answer:
- Aggregate turnover means the aggregate value of all taxable supplies (excluding the value of inward supplies on which tax is payable under reverse charge), exempt supplies, exports of goods or services, and inter-State supplies of persons having the same PAN, computed on an all-India basis.
- It excludes CGST, SGST, UTGST, IGST and cess.
- Exempt supply includes nil-rated, wholly exempt and non-taxable supplies (such as alcoholic liquor), so they are included.
- Schedule III activities are not supplies and are excluded.
- Relevance: registration threshold (section 22), composition eligibility (section 10), QRMP and e-invoicing thresholds, annual return and reconciliation requirements, and HSN digit requirements on invoices.

chapters.title: Tax Invoice, Credit and Debit Notes, E-way Bill
chapters.summary: When and how to issue a tax invoice or bill of supply, e-invoicing, credit and debit notes under section 34, and the e-way bill system under rule 138.
chapters.lawAsOf: CGST Act sections 31, 34 and 68 and CGST Rules 46 to 55A and 138 to 138E, as amended by the Finance Act 2026

lesson.heading: Tax invoice: section 31
lesson.body:
| Supply | Time limit for invoice |
| --- | --- |
| Goods involving movement | Before or at the time of **removal** for supply |
| Goods not involving movement | Before or at the time of **delivery** or making available |
| Continuous supply of goods | Before or at the time of each successive statement of account or payment |
| Services | Before or after provision, within **30 days** of supply (45 days for banks, insurers, financial institutions and NBFCs) - rule 47 |

Other documents:
- **Bill of supply** for exempt supplies and by composition taxpayers (section 31(3)(c)). A tax invoice and bill of supply can be combined where both taxable and exempt goods are supplied to an unregistered person.
- **Receipt voucher** on receipt of an advance; **refund voucher** if no supply is made after an advance.
- **Self-invoice** by a registered recipient paying tax under RCM on supplies from an unregistered supplier, and a **payment voucher** when paying the supplier.
- **Consolidated invoice:** where the value of supply is below ₹200 and the recipient is unregistered and does not ask for an invoice, a consolidated invoice may be issued at the end of each day.

Rule 46 contents include: supplier's name, address and GSTIN; a consecutive serial number up to 16 characters, unique for a financial year; date; recipient's name, address and GSTIN if registered; for an unregistered recipient, name, address and delivery address where the value is ₹50,000 or more; HSN or SAC code; description, quantity, value, rate and tax amounts; place of supply with State name for inter-State supplies; whether tax is payable on reverse charge; signature.

HSN digits: 4 digits if aggregate turnover in the preceding FY is up to ₹5 crore; 6 digits above ₹5 crore.

Copies (rule 48): goods - triplicate (original for recipient, duplicate for transporter, triplicate for supplier); services - duplicate.

lesson.heading: E-invoicing
lesson.body:
A registered person whose aggregate turnover in any financial year from 2017-18 onward exceeds **₹5 crore** must generate e-invoices for B2B supplies and exports by uploading invoice details to the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP). The IRP returns a unique **Invoice Reference Number (IRN)**, digitally signs the invoice and generates a QR code. An invoice without a valid IRN, where e-invoicing applies, is not a valid invoice.

Exempt from e-invoicing: SEZ units, insurers, banking companies, financial institutions and NBFCs, GTAs, suppliers of passenger transport services, and suppliers of admission to cinema exhibitions in multiplex screens. Government departments and local authorities are also excluded.

E-invoice data flows automatically to GSTR-1 and, where details are given, to Part A of the e-way bill.

lesson.heading: Credit notes and debit notes: section 34
lesson.body:
| Point | Credit note | Debit note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| When issued | Taxable value or tax in the invoice exceeds the correct amount; goods returned; goods or services found deficient. Finance Act 2026 adds post-supply discounts under the substituted section 15(3)(b) as an express ground | Taxable value or tax in the invoice is less than the correct amount |
| Effect | Reduces supplier's output tax; recipient reverses ITC | Increases supplier's output tax |
| Time limit | Must be declared in the return not later than **30 November** following the end of the FY of supply, or the date of filing the annual return, whichever is earlier | No time limit for issue; recipient's ITC time limit under section 16(4) runs from the FY of the debit note |
| Condition | Supplier's output tax is reduced only if the incidence of tax has not been passed on to any other person | - |

One credit or debit note can cover several invoices of a financial year.

lesson.heading: E-way bill: rule 138
lesson.body:
Every registered person who causes **movement of goods** of consignment value exceeding **₹50,000** must generate an e-way bill (EWB) before movement, whether the movement is in relation to a supply, for reasons other than supply (such as branch transfer or job work), or due to an inward supply from an unregistered person.

**Consignment value** is the value under section 15 shown in the invoice, bill of supply or delivery challan, **including** GST and cess, but **excluding** the value of exempt supplies where the invoice covers both.

**Mandatory irrespective of value:** inter-State movement of goods by a principal to a job worker, and inter-State transport of handicraft goods by a person exempt from registration.

**Part A** has GSTIN of recipient, place of delivery, document number and date, value, HSN and reason for transport. **Part B** has the vehicle number. Part B is not required where goods move up to **50 km** within the same State from the consignor's place of business to the transporter's place of business, or from the transporter's place to the consignee's place.

**Not required (examples):** goods in the exempt list (such as fresh vegetables and fruits); goods moved by a non-motorised conveyance; goods moved from a port, airport, air cargo complex or land customs station to an inland container depot or container freight station for customs clearance; goods under customs seal or customs supervision; transit cargo to or from Nepal or Bhutan.

**Validity (rule 138(10)):**

| Cargo | Validity |
| --- | --- |
| Normal cargo | 1 day for up to 200 km, plus 1 day for every additional 200 km or part |
| Over dimensional cargo or multimodal shipment with ship | 1 day for up to 20 km, plus 1 day for every additional 20 km or part |

A day ends at midnight of the day following the date of generation. An EWB can be cancelled within **24 hours** of generation (not if verified in transit); the recipient may reject it within 72 hours.

**Worked example:** a normal consignment travels 640 km. Validity = 1 day (first 200 km) + 3 days (440 km, i.e. 2 full blocks of 200 km and 40 km part) = **4 days**.

**Common mistakes:** excluding GST from consignment value; ignoring the job work rule for low-value consignments; counting validity from dispatch rather than generation.

keyPoints: Goods invoice: at or before removal; services invoice: within 30 days (45 days for banks, insurers, NBFCs).
Bill of supply for exempt supplies and composition dealers; self-invoice for RCM purchases from unregistered persons.
Invoice serial number: up to 16 characters, unique per FY; HSN 4 digits up to ₹5 crore turnover, 6 digits above.
E-invoicing (IRN from IRP): aggregate turnover above ₹5 crore in any FY from 2017-18.
Credit note: declare by the earlier of 30 November after FY end and annual return filing; recipient reverses ITC.
E-way bill: consignment value above ₹50,000 including tax, excluding exempt goods; job work inter-State always.
Validity: 1 day per 200 km (normal), 1 day per 20 km (ODC); cancel within 24 hours; Part B not needed up to 50 km within a State.

cases.title: Case: Om Steel Traders
cases.body:
Om Steel Traders, Nagpur (Maharashtra), a registered dealer, sells steel sections to Malwa Fabricators, a registered buyer in Indore (Madhya Pradesh).

| Date | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 15 October 2026 | Invoice for taxable value ₹2,50,000 + IGST @ 18% ₹45,000 = ₹2,95,000. Goods dispatched by a hired truck (normal cargo); road distance 640 km |
| 25 October 2026 | Malwa returns defective goods of taxable value ₹40,000 |

Om's aggregate turnover in the previous FY was ₹3.2 crore and it has never exceeded ₹5 crore.

questions.prompt: By when must a tax invoice be issued for a supply of goods that involves movement?
options: Within 30 days of removal
Before or at the time of removal of goods for supply
At the time of receipt of payment
By the 10th of the next month
questions.explanation: Section 31(1)(a): for goods involving movement, the invoice is issued before or at the time of removal for supply to the recipient. The 30-day limit applies to services.

questions.prompt: Which of the following persons is exempt from issuing e-invoices even if aggregate turnover exceeds ₹5 crore?
options: A steel manufacturer
A banking company
A software exporter
A pharmaceutical distributor
questions.explanation: Insurers, banking companies, financial institutions including NBFCs, GTAs, passenger transport suppliers, multiplex admission suppliers and SEZ units are excluded from e-invoicing.

questions.prompt: How many copies of a tax invoice are prepared for a supply of goods?
options: Two
Three
Four
One original only
questions.explanation: Rule 48(1): goods - triplicate (original for recipient, duplicate for transporter, triplicate for supplier). Rule 48(2): services - duplicate.

questions.prompt: A composition taxpayer must issue a tax invoice showing CGST and SGST separately.
questions.explanation: A composition taxpayer cannot collect tax and issues a bill of supply under section 31(3)(c), with the declaration 'composition taxable person, not eligible to collect tax on supplies'.

questions.prompt: Fill the blank: on uploading an e-invoice, the Invoice Registration Portal generates a unique ___ (abbreviation) for each invoice.
questions.explanation: The IRP validates the invoice, generates the Invoice Reference Number (IRN), digitally signs it and adds a QR code.

questions.prompt: A dealer sends one consignment with a single invoice: taxable goods ₹40,000 + GST @ 18%, and exempt goods (fresh fruits) ₹20,000. Compute the consignment value for e-way bill purposes. Round to the nearest rupee.
questions.explanation:
Consignment value includes GST but excludes exempt supplies covered in the same invoice.

| Particulars | ₹ |
| --- | --- |
| Taxable goods | 40,000 |
| GST @ 18% | 7,200 |
| Exempt goods | Excluded |
| **Consignment value** | **47,200** |

It does not exceed ₹50,000, so no e-way bill is required.

questions.prompt: An over dimensional cargo moves 85 km. Compute the validity of the e-way bill in days.
questions.explanation:
For over dimensional cargo: 1 day for up to 20 km plus 1 day for every additional 20 km or part.

| Distance | Days |
| --- | --- |
| First 20 km | 1 |
| Next 65 km = 3 full blocks of 20 km + 5 km part | 4 |
| **Total** | **5** |

questions.prompt: In which of these cases is an e-way bill NOT required? Select all that apply.
options: Goods moved by a bullock cart, value ₹2,00,000
Inter-State movement of goods worth ₹30,000 from principal to job worker
Fresh vegetables worth ₹1,20,000
Taxable goods of value ₹50,000 plus GST of ₹9,000 moved by truck
Goods under customs seal moving from port to an inland container depot
questions.explanation: Non-motorised conveyance, exempt goods such as fresh vegetables, and goods under customs seal are excluded. Inter-State job work movement needs an EWB irrespective of value, and ₹59,000 (including tax) exceeds ₹50,000.

questions.prompt: Is an e-way bill required for the 15 October dispatch, and is an e-invoice required?
options: EWB required; e-invoice not required
EWB not required; e-invoice required
Both required
Neither required
questions.explanation: Consignment value ₹2,95,000 exceeds ₹50,000, so an EWB is required. Om's aggregate turnover has never exceeded ₹5 crore, so e-invoicing does not apply.

questions.prompt: Compute the validity of the e-way bill in days for the Nagpur to Indore journey.
questions.explanation:
Normal cargo: 1 day up to 200 km, plus 1 day for every additional 200 km or part.

| Distance | Days |
| --- | --- |
| First 200 km | 1 |
| Next 440 km = 2 full blocks of 200 km + 40 km part | 3 |
| **Total** | **4** |

questions.prompt: Om issues a credit note for the goods returned on 25 October 2026. Compute the IGST to be shown in the credit note. Round to the nearest rupee.
questions.explanation:
| Particulars | ₹ |
| --- | --- |
| Taxable value of goods returned | 40,000 |
| IGST @ 18% | 7,200 |

Om reduces its output tax by ₹7,200 (the incidence is not passed on, as the buyer reverses its ITC). The credit note must be declared by the earlier of 30 November 2027 and the date of filing the annual return for FY 2026-27.

questions.prompt: State whether an e-way bill is required in each case and, if so, whether Part B must be filled. All movements are by registered persons.
questions.data:
- (a) Intra-State supply of taxable goods: value ₹45,000 + GST ₹8,100, by truck.
- (b) Fresh vegetables worth ₹1,20,000 by truck.
- (c) Inter-State movement of parts worth ₹30,000 to a job worker.
- (d) Goods worth ₹2,00,000 delivered by a bullock cart.
- (e) Taxable goods worth ₹3,00,000 moved from the factory to the transporter's godown 30 km away in the same State, for onward inter-State transport.
questions.answer:
| Case | EWB required? | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) | Yes | Consignment value including tax ₹53,100 exceeds ₹50,000 |
| (b) | No | Fresh vegetables are in the list of goods exempt from EWB |
| (c) | Yes | Inter-State movement to a job worker needs EWB irrespective of value |
| (d) | No | Movement by non-motorised conveyance |
| (e) | Yes, Part A; Part B not required for this leg | Movement up to 50 km within the State from consignor to transporter's place; Part B is updated when the goods leave the transporter's godown |

questions.prompt: Explain the circumstances in which a credit note may be issued under section 34 and the time limit for declaring it.
questions.answer:
- A registered supplier may issue a credit note where: the taxable value or tax charged in the invoice exceeds the correct amount; goods supplied are returned by the recipient; goods or services supplied are found deficient. The Finance Act 2026 also adds post-supply discounts under the substituted section 15(3)(b).
- One credit note may cover one or more invoices of a financial year.
- The details must be declared in the return for the month in which it is issued, and not later than 30 November following the end of the FY in which the supply was made, or the date of filing the annual return, whichever is earlier.
- The supplier's output tax is reduced only if the incidence of tax has not been passed on to any other person.
- The recipient must reverse ITC to the extent of the credit note.

questions.prompt: Who generates the e-way bill and what are Part A and Part B? Explain with reference to movement by the supplier, the recipient and a transporter.
questions.answer:
- The registered person causing movement of goods (consignor or consignee) generates the EWB in Form EWB-01 before movement, where consignment value exceeds ₹50,000.
- Part A: GSTIN of recipient, place of delivery (PIN), document number and date, value of goods, HSN code and reason for transportation.
- Part B: transport document number and vehicle number.
- If the registered person moves goods in his own or hired conveyance, he fills Parts A and B.
- If goods are handed to a transporter, the registered person fills Part A and the transporter can fill Part B; if the registered person does not generate the EWB, the transporter generates it on the basis of the information in Part A.
- Where an unregistered supplier supplies to a registered recipient, the recipient is treated as the person causing movement and complies.
- Part B is not needed for movement up to 50 km within the same State to or from the transporter's place of business.

chapters.title: Accounts and Records, Payment of Tax and Returns
chapters.summary: Accounts and records under sections 35 and 36, the electronic ledgers, order of ITC utilisation, interest under section 50, and the GST return cycle including QRMP and annual returns.
chapters.lawAsOf: CGST Act sections 35, 36, 37 to 48, 49, 49A, 49B and 50, and related rules, as amended by the Finance Act 2026

lesson.heading: Accounts and records: sections 35 and 36
lesson.body:
Every registered person keeps, at his **principal place of business** (and for each additional place, the records relating to it), a true and correct account of production or manufacture, inward and outward supplies, stock, ITC availed, output tax payable and paid, and other prescribed particulars. Records may be kept electronically.

- Owners or operators of warehouses, godowns and transporters keep records of consignor, consignee and goods, whether or not registered.
- Records must be retained for **72 months** from the **due date of the annual return** for the year to which they relate (section 36).
- If the person is party to an appeal, revision or proceedings, records are kept for one year after final disposal, or the 72-month period, whichever is later.
- Unaccounted goods found at the place of business are deemed supplied, and tax is determined on them.

lesson.heading: Electronic ledgers and utilisation of ITC: sections 49, 49A, 49B, rule 88A
lesson.body:
| Ledger | What it holds | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Electronic cash ledger | Deposits via PMT-06 by internet banking, NEFT/RTGS, cards, or over the counter (up to ₹10,000 per challan per tax period) | Tax (forward and reverse charge), interest, penalty, fee and other amounts |
| Electronic credit ledger | ITC self-assessed in returns | **Output tax** under forward charge only; not interest, penalty, fee or RCM tax |
| Electronic liability register | All liabilities | Record of dues |

Date of deposit is the date the amount is credited to the Government account. Amounts in the cash ledger can be transferred between heads (PMT-09) and, subject to conditions, to the cash ledger of a distinct person with the same PAN.

**Order of utilisation of ITC:**

| Credit of | First against | Then against | Never against |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| IGST | IGST | CGST and SGST/UTGST, in any order and proportion | - |
| CGST | CGST | IGST | SGST/UTGST |
| SGST/UTGST | SGST/UTGST | IGST (only after CGST credit is exhausted for IGST) | CGST |

IGST credit must be **fully** used before CGST or SGST credit is used (section 49A, rule 88A).

**Order of discharge (section 49(8)):** (a) self-assessed tax and other dues for previous periods; (b) self-assessed tax and other dues for the current period; (c) any other amount, including demands under sections 73 and 74.

**Rule 86B:** a registered person whose taxable supplies (other than exempt and zero-rated) exceed ₹50 lakh in a month must pay at least 1% of output tax in cash, subject to exceptions (such as income tax above ₹1 lakh paid in each of the last two years, or refund of more than ₹1 lakh received on account of exports).

lesson.heading: Interest: section 50
lesson.body:
| Situation | Rate | Period and base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tax not paid or paid late - 50(1) | 18% p.a. | From the day after the due date until payment. For tax paid late with a return filed after the due date, interest is only on the portion paid through the **cash ledger** (not if the return is filed after proceedings under section 73 or 74 have begun) |
| ITC wrongly availed **and utilised** - 50(3) | 18% p.a. (reduced from 24% retrospectively from 1 July 2017 by the Finance Act 2022) | From the date of utilisation to the date of reversal or payment (rule 88B) |

Interest is calculated on a daily basis: Amount x 18% x days / 365. ITC wrongly availed but not utilised does not attract interest.

lesson.heading: Returns and due dates
lesson.body:
| Return | Who | Frequency | Due date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GSTR-1 | Normal taxpayers: outward supplies | Monthly / quarterly (QRMP) | 11th of next month / 13th of month after quarter |
| IFF | QRMP taxpayers: B2B invoices for first two months (optional) | Monthly | 13th of next month |
| GSTR-3B | Normal taxpayers: summary return with payment | Monthly / quarterly (QRMP) | 20th of next month / 22nd or 24th of month after quarter, by State |
| CMP-08 | Composition taxpayers: statement of tax | Quarterly | 18th of month after quarter |
| GSTR-4 | Composition taxpayers | Annual | 30 April after FY end |
| GSTR-5 | Non-resident taxable persons | Monthly | 13th of next month |
| GSTR-6 | Input Service Distributor | Monthly | 13th of next month |
| GSTR-7 / GSTR-8 | TDS deductors / ECOs collecting TCS | Monthly | 10th of next month |
| GSTR-9 | Annual return (optional if aggregate turnover up to ₹2 crore) | Annual | 31 December after FY end |
| GSTR-9C | Self-certified reconciliation statement (aggregate turnover above ₹5 crore) | Annual | With GSTR-9 |
| GSTR-10 | Final return on cancellation | Once | Within 3 months of cancellation |

**QRMP scheme:** for aggregate turnover up to ₹5 crore. Quarterly GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B, but tax is paid monthly by the 25th of the next month for the first two months in PMT-06, by either the **fixed sum method** (35% of tax paid in cash in the preceding quarter where returns were quarterly, or 100% of cash paid in the last month of the preceding quarter where filed monthly) or the **self-assessment method** (actual liability less ITC).

Other rules: a return cannot be filed if a previous return is not filed (section 39(10)); GSTR-3B cannot be filed if GSTR-1 for the period is not filed (section 39(10)); returns cannot be filed after **3 years** from the due date (sections 37(4), 39(11), 44(2), inserted by the Finance Act 2023). Late fee applies under section 47.

keyPoints: Records kept at the principal place of business, retained 72 months from the due date of the annual return.
Credit ledger pays only forward-charge output tax; RCM tax, interest, penalty and fee are paid in cash.
Utilisation: IGST credit first and fully (IGST, then CGST/SGST in any proportion); CGST to CGST then IGST; SGST to SGST then IGST; never CGST against SGST.
Interest 18% under section 50(1) on net cash liability for late returns; 18% under 50(3) on ITC wrongly availed and utilised.
Due dates: GSTR-1 11th, GSTR-3B 20th, CMP-08 18th, GSTR-4 30 April, GSTR-9 31 December.
QRMP: turnover up to ₹5 crore; monthly PMT-06 by 25th; fixed sum 35% of last quarter's cash tax.
No return can be filed after 3 years from its due date.

cases.title: Case: Nirmal Exports Pvt Ltd
cases.body:
Nirmal Exports Pvt Ltd, Pune, files monthly returns. For August 2026, all liabilities are under forward charge.

| Particulars | CGST (₹) | SGST (₹) | IGST (₹) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Output tax liability | 80,000 | 80,000 | 1,50,000 |
| ITC available (opening balance + eligible credit for the month) | 50,000 | 40,000 | 1,20,000 |

GSTR-3B for August 2026 was due on 20 September 2026. The company filed it, and paid the cash portion, on 5 October 2026.

questions.prompt: For how long must a registered person retain books of account for FY 2025-26, whose annual return was due on 31 December 2026?
options: Until 31 March 2032
Until 31 December 2032
Until 31 December 2031
Six years from the end of FY 2025-26
questions.explanation: Section 36: 72 months (6 years) from the due date of the annual return for the year. 31 December 2026 plus 72 months is 31 December 2032.

questions.prompt: Which of the following can be paid by debiting the electronic credit ledger?
options: Interest under section 50
Late fee under section 47
Output CGST under forward charge
GST payable under reverse charge
questions.explanation: Section 49(4): the credit ledger may be used only for output tax. The Explanation to section 49 defines tax dues to exclude interest, penalty and fee, and RCM tax must be paid in cash.

questions.prompt: Which statement about utilisation of ITC is correct?
options: CGST credit can be used to pay SGST
IGST credit must be fully utilised before CGST or SGST credit is used
SGST credit must be used first against IGST
IGST credit can be used only against IGST
questions.explanation: Section 49A and rule 88A: IGST credit is first used against IGST and the balance against CGST and SGST in any order and proportion; it must be exhausted before CGST/SGST credit is used. Cross-utilisation between CGST and SGST is not allowed.

questions.prompt: What is the due date of the annual return GSTR-9 for FY 2026-27?
options: 30 November 2027
31 December 2027
30 April 2027
30 September 2027
questions.explanation: Section 44 read with rule 80: GSTR-9 is due by 31 December following the end of the financial year. GSTR-9 is optional for aggregate turnover up to ₹2 crore.

questions.prompt: A taxpayer can file a GSTR-3B return for a period five years after its due date, on payment of late fee.
questions.explanation: Sections 37(4), 39(11) and 44(2), inserted by the Finance Act 2023, bar filing of GSTR-1, GSTR-3B and the annual return after three years from the due date (subject to notified relaxations).

questions.prompt: Fill the blank: a composition taxpayer files the quarterly statement for payment of tax in Form GST CMP-08 by the ___ day of the month following the quarter.
questions.explanation: CMP-08 is due by the 18th of the month after the quarter; the annual GSTR-4 is due by 30 April after the financial year.

questions.prompt: Which of the following must be paid only through the electronic cash ledger? Select all that apply.
options: Tax payable under reverse charge
Interest under section 50
Late fee under section 47
Output IGST under forward charge
Penalty
questions.explanation: RCM tax, interest, late fee and penalty are paid in cash. Only forward-charge output tax can be paid from the credit ledger.

questions.prompt: A registered person wrongly availed ITC of ₹1,00,000, which was utilised for 73 days before he reversed it. Compute interest under section 50(3). Round to the nearest rupee.
questions.explanation:
Interest at 18% p.a. applies to ITC wrongly availed and utilised, from the date of utilisation to reversal.

| Particulars | ₹ |
| --- | --- |
| 1,00,000 x 18% x 73 / 365 | 3,600 |

questions.prompt: A QRMP taxpayer filed quarterly GSTR-3B for April-June and paid ₹1,20,000 of tax in cash for that quarter. Under the fixed sum method, compute the amount to be paid in PMT-06 for July. Round to the nearest rupee.
questions.explanation:
Fixed sum method: 35% of the tax paid in cash in the preceding quarter where the return was furnished quarterly.

| Particulars | ₹ |
| --- | --- |
| 35% of 1,20,000 | 42,000 |

questions.prompt: Compute the minimum amount Nirmal Exports must pay through the electronic cash ledger for August 2026 (tax only, excluding interest). Round to the nearest rupee.
questions.explanation:
| Step | CGST | SGST | IGST |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Liability | 80,000 | 80,000 | 1,50,000 |

questions.prompt: Explain the three electronic ledgers maintained on the GST portal and their purpose.
questions.answer:
- Electronic cash ledger (section 49(1)): credited with deposits made through PMT-06 by internet banking, NEFT/RTGS, cards or over the counter (up to ₹10,000 per challan). Used for payment of tax (including RCM), interest, penalty, fee and other amounts. Balance can be refunded or transferred between heads and to distinct persons with the same PAN, subject to conditions.
- Electronic credit ledger (section 49(2)): credited with self-assessed ITC as per the return. Used only for output tax under forward charge, in the order laid down in sections 49, 49A, 49B and rule 88A.
- Electronic liability register: records all liabilities - return-based tax, interest, late fee, and demands - and is debited when payments are made from the cash or credit ledger.
- The date of deposit in the cash ledger is the date the amount is credited to the Government account.

questions.prompt: What is the QRMP scheme? Explain the eligibility and the methods of monthly payment of tax.
questions.answer:
- Quarterly Return Monthly Payment scheme for registered persons with aggregate turnover up to ₹5 crore in the preceding FY (and in the current FY), who are required to file GSTR-3B.
- They file GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B quarterly; B2B invoices for the first two months may be uploaded through the optional Invoice Furnishing Facility (IFF) by the 13th of the next month.
- Tax for the first two months of a quarter is paid by the 25th of the next month in PMT-06.
- Fixed sum method: 35% of tax paid in cash in the preceding quarter (if returns were quarterly) or 100% of cash tax paid in the last month of the preceding quarter (if returns were monthly). No payment if the amount is nil.
- Self-assessment method: actual liability for the month less ITC available.
- Amounts deposited are adjusted against the quarterly GSTR-3B; interest applies if the self-assessed method shows short payment.
- The option is exercised per GSTIN and can be changed for a future quarter.
